title: Sol Ultra Cycle Double Cover proof gets a Lean formalization verdict by Q1 2027
body: OpenAI's July 10 proof PDF for the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture — authored entirely by GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra orchestrating up to 64 parallel subagents — arrives with the decisive caveat that it has not been formalized in Lean or any proof assistant and has not passed community review. That gap will not stay open long. The claim is high-stakes in both directions: if the argument holds, it is the strongest evidence yet that orchestrated subagent swarms outperform single-model reasoning at frontier research, and OpenAI has every incentive to fund and publicize a machine-checkable formalization; if it breaks, graph theorists who have worked the 1979 Seymour problem for decades have every incentive to publish the counterexample or gap analysis quickly. Lean's mathlib community has repeatedly turned headline claims into formalization sprints within months, and adversarial-verification subagents were already part of the original run design, so the proof text itself is structured for mechanical checking. The prediction: within two quarters the claim resolves publicly one way or the other — either a substantially complete Lean formalization effort validates the core argument, or named mathematicians publish a specific, acknowledged flaw. A quiet indefinite limbo is the least likely outcome given the attention the result has drawn.

reasoning.plain_language: A computer says it solved a 50-year-old math puzzle; mathematicians will now check the work, and we should know soon whether it is right.

Expect either Lean formalization progress validating the argument or a published flaw from named graph theorists by Q1 2027; indefinite limbo is unlikely.
